rules: 1. The new it() is named exactly 'should resolve deferred page routes for app root elements during bootstrap' and is async; it sits inside describe('prepareSpecializedApp') right after the 'should synchronously finalize feature flag predicates without sign-in' case, with one blank line before it.

2. Build the app plugin as that neighbouring case does: appPluginOriginal.withOverrides with appPluginOriginal.getExtension('sign-in-page:app').override({ disabled: true }), so the bootstrap does not require sign-in and finalize() is synchronous.

3. Declare const fooRouteRef = createRouteRef(); and a createFrontendPlugin({ pluginId: 'test', extensions: [...] }) with two createExtension calls: name 'foo-page' attached to { id: 'app/routes', input: 'routes' } with output [coreExtensionData.routePath, coreExtensionData.routeRef, coreExtensionData.reactElement] yielding routePath('/foo'), routeRef(fooRouteRef) and reactElement(
Foo Page

link: {link?.() ?? 'none'}

behaviour: extractRouteInfoFromAppNode accepts an optional map of fallback instances that supplies route data for nodes that have no instance of their own.
rules: 1. Add a third optional parameter fallbackInstances?: ReadonlyMap<AppNode, AppNodeInstance> after routeAliasResolver; the existing two-argument callers and tests keep working unchanged.

2. In visit, read const instance = current.instance ?? fallbackInstances?.get(current); and take both routePath and foundRouteRef from instance instead of current.instance; every other line of the walk stays as it is.
3. A node's own instance always wins over a fallback instance, so a call without the third argument produces exactly the RouteInfo it produces today.

sites.rule: Add the optional fallbackInstances parameter per rule 1, with a one-line comment above the function saying it supplies route data for nodes that are not instantiated yet, such as the deferred app/root.children subtree during bootstrap.
Introduce the instance local per rule 2 and read routePath (with the same leading-slash strip) and foundRouteRef from it.

behaviour: Bootstrap route resolution includes route paths and refs from the deferred app/root.children subtree, and route functions handed out before finalization follow the finalized resolver.
rules: 1. Add a module-level const EMPTY_API_HOLDER: ApiHolder = { get() { return undefined; } }; and a non-exported function collectDeferredRouteInstances(options: { tree: AppTree; extensionFactoryMiddleware?: ExtensionFactoryMiddleware; stopAtAttachment(ctx: { node: AppNode; input: string }): boolean }): Map<AppNode, AppNodeInstance>, both placed between instantiateAndInitializePhaseTree and setIdentityApiTarget.

2. collectDeferredRouteInstances walks from options.tree.root over node.edges.attachments with a visited Set; for each input where options.stopAtAttachment({ node, input }) is true, every child of that input is handed to the deferred visit instead of the normal walk.

3. The deferred visit, with its own visited Set, skips a node and its whole subtree when node.spec.disabled is true or node.spec.if !== undefined (predicate-gated pages are only resolvable after finalization).

4. For any other deferred node that has no instance and whose extension declares a coreExtensionData.routePath or coreExtensionData.routeRef output, call instantiateAppNodeSubtree({ rootNode: node, apis: EMPTY_API_HOLDER, collector: createErrorCollector(), extensionFactoryMiddleware: options.extensionFactoryMiddleware, writeNodeInstances: false, reuseExistingInstances: false }) and, when the result has an instance, store it in the map under the original node; a failed instantiation is ignored and leaves the node out.

5. Detect declared outputs with toInternalExtension(node.spec.extension): for version 'v1' look at Object.values(internal.output), for 'v2' at internal.output, comparing each ref.id with coreExtensionData.routePath.id and coreExtensionData.routeRef.id; nodes without such outputs are never instantiated, so app/layout, app/routes and other content factories do not run during bootstrap.
6. The deferred visit then continues into every child of every input of the node, so nested pages and sub-pages are collected too.

7. In instantiateAndInitializePhaseTree pass the result of collectDeferredRouteInstances({ tree, extensionFactoryMiddleware, stopAtAttachment }) as the third argument of extractRouteInfoFromAppNode only when options.stopAtAttachment is set, and undefined otherwise, so finalization extracts route info exactly as before.

8. RouteResolutionApiProxy.resolve keeps its existing throw when #delegate is unset; otherwise it captures const delegate = this.#delegate, calls delegate.resolve(anyRouteRef, options), and returns undefined when that is undefined.

9. Otherwise resolve returns a new RouteFunc<TParams> that calls the captured function while this.#delegate is still the captured delegate; once the proxy has been re-initialized it resolves the same anyRouteRef and options against the current delegate, caches that result together with the delegate it came from inside the closure, and calls it, falling back to the captured function when the current delegate returns undefined.

10. Add one or two short why-comments: one at the deferred-route collection explaining bootstrap stops at the session boundary while app root elements still need those routes, one at the resolve wrapper explaining useRouteRef memoizes on the proxy instance, which keeps its identity across finalization.
